                    ### Question
                    A 48-year-old man comes to the physician for the evaluation of dyspnea and cough. He was diagnosed with esophageal cancer 10 months ago, for which he received radiochemotherapy. He has a history of atopic dermatitis and has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 30 years. Auscultation of the lungs shows decreased breath sounds bilaterally. Spirometry shows an FVC of 78% and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 95%. Which of the following is the most likely underlying condition?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Chronic bronchitis
opb. Pulmonary emphysema
opc. Allergic asthma
opd. Pulmonary fibrosis
ope. Pulmonary embolism

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient has a history of esophageal cancer and received radiochemotherapy, which can lead to lung damage, potentially causing pulmonary fibrosis. His symptoms of dyspnea and cough, along with decreased breath sounds bilaterally and spirometry results showing an FVC of 78% and an FEV1/FVC ratio of 95%, suggest a restrictive lung pattern rather than obstructive. The preserved FEV1/FVC ratio indicates that the primary issue is not obstructive lung disease (like chronic bronchitis or emphysema). The history of smoking increases the risk for lung disease but does not directly correlate with the restrictive pattern observed. Therefore, the most likely underlying condition is pulmonary fibrosis, likely related to the previous cancer treatment.
